suggestions.assertion: Defines a port interface in vendor/shared/adapters.ts before/alongside the concrete client
suggestions.reason: All four runs satisfied this identically. The assertion is satisfied by ANY exported interface added to adapters.ts; it does not check that the port is free of vendor-specific types. Three of the four plans (with_skill/run-1 `IssueTracker`, with_skill/run-2 `IssueTrackerClient`, without_skill/run-1 `TicketClient`) claim vendor neutrality in prose yet pin `readonly id: 'linear'` / `readonly provider: 'linear'` into the interface, so a Jira adapter could not implement the port without widening it. An assertion like 'the port interface contains no Linear-specific literal type or field' would discriminate.

suggestions.assertion: The route handler contains no business branching and no direct data access
suggestions.reason: Every plan wrote a ~15-line handler that is Zod schema + getContext + one service call, so this passes for all four. It would be more discriminating to assert on the whole diff — e.g. 'no route file in the change imports db/schema.js or drizzle-orm' — because two plans (with_skill/run-2, without_skill/run-2) DO add a new `if (provider === LINEAR_PROVIDER)` branch plus a live external call to the existing `POST /settings/test-connection` handler in modules/settings/routes.ts. That is consistent with the pre-existing GitHub branch in that file, but the current assertion is blind to it.

The whole assertion set is non-discriminating for this eval: all four runs (both with_skill and both without_skill) pass 7/7 and satisfy 8/8 expected_steps. The assertions describe the correct answer at a granularity the base model already reaches unaided in this repo, which has GitHubClient/OctokitGitHubClient as a directly analogous, highly imitable precedent one grep away. To measure the skill, the assertions need to target the decisions where the plans actually diverged: whether the adapter subfolder is named for the vendor (`adapters/linear/`) or for the domain (`adapters/tickets/`); whether the container accessor throws ConfigError (3 runs) or returns a typed `null` (with_skill/run-1); whether the new file set stays inside `server/` as the prompt scoped it (with_skill/run-1 also writes two files under `client/src/vendor/shared/`); and whether cached ticket state gets a new table + migration (3 runs) or is recomputed per request (with_skill/run-1).

suggestions.assertion: Wires the adapter into platform/container.ts including a ContainerOverrides field
suggestions.reason: Passes on the presence of any field. It does not check that the container is the ONLY constructor of the adapter — which is the actual onion rule and the thing most likely to be got wrong. 'No file other than platform/container.ts and adapters/index.ts imports the concrete client class' would be a stronger, still-mechanical check (all four happened to satisfy it here).

eval_feedback.overall: All seven assertions pass on genuine, inspected code, and this run matches the answer key's file paths more literally than either with_skill run (`adapters/linear/graphql.ts`). Since it scores 7/7 and 8/8 without the skill, the assertion set gives no signal about the skill's contribution.
